title: Functorial ordinary base-derived tensor cohomology
statement: Let R, A, B, C be commutative rings in universe u, A and B R-algebras, and C an E=A tensor_R B algebra. Assume derived categories for modules over R and B [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For every A-complex P [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], let m(P) be its canonical BaseDerivedTensorCohomologyModel R A B P C [def-pc-base-derived-tensor-cohomology-model]. Fix an integer i. There are a functor H from all A-module cochain complexes to E-modules, a natural transformation sigma from H to degree-i homology of ordinary extension A-to-E, and isomorphisms e(P):m(P).cohomology(i) to H(P), such that H inverts every quasi-isomorphism and e(P).hom followed by sigma(P) equals m(P).comparison(i). No extension of the source from E to C, tensor with a second complex, or localized comparison is asserted.

proof.text: For each chain map apply lem-pc-base-derived-tensor-cohomology-model-map. The target universal counit identifies its derived transformation with the canonical leftDerivedNatTrans induced by the identity. The model-map equation and faithful B-restriction, followed by cancellation of cohomologyIso, determine the E-linear map uniquely. Use these uniquely determined maps between the actual canonical model cohomology objects.

The identities leftDerivedNatTrans_id and leftDerivedNatTrans_comp and naturality show the chosen maps obey the functor laws after faithful restriction. Exact A-to-R restriction preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Derived localization, the model derived functor and homology preserve the resulting isomorphisms; the canonical comparison of universal derived functors is invertible. The model-map equation and reflection by restriction prove H inverts quasi-isomorphisms. Take e to be the identity isomorphism of the model cohomology object.

Use model.comparison as the components of sigma. Check naturality of model.ordinaryIso on 1 tensor p, then extend by tensor induction. Restrict the proposed comparison square to B and compose with the inverse restriction homology isomorphism. Rewrite comparison_eq and the model-map equation. Apply counit compatibility and counit naturality, naturality of the derived and homotopy homology factorization isomorphisms, and the ordinaryIso square. Faithfulness and cancellation prove the E-linear comparison square, hence sigma is natural. The component equation is identity composition.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_baseTensorCohomologyFunctor (i : ℤ) :
    let m := fun P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ ↦
      baseDerivedTensorCohomologyModel R A B P C
    let E := (extendScalars.{u, u, u} (algebraMap A (A ⊗[R] B))).mapHomologicalComplex
      (.up ℤ)
    ∃ (H : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} (A ⊗[R] B))
      (σ : H ⟶ E ⋙ HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} (A ⊗[R] B))
        (.up ℤ) i)
      (e : ∀ P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ, (m P).cohomology i ≅ H.obj P),
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{u} A) (.up ℤ)).IsInvertedBy H ∧
      ∀ P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ,
        (e P).hom ≫ σ.app P = (m P).comparison i
